standfirst: The WSET Level 1 Award in Beer is short enough that a late start is not a lost cause. Here is what the exam asks, where late starters drop marks and how our in-person training in four cities closes the gap.
sections: Six hours of guided learning is short enough to start this week

The Wine & Spirit Education Trust (WSET) sets the Level 1 Award in Beer at six hours of guided learning. That figure includes the 45-minute exam. WSET describes the course as fully guided, with no private study expected on top. In plain terms, this is a qualification you can still prepare for properly if your exam is a week or two away.

That is why we run last-minute training for it. We teach it in person in Pune, Delhi, Gurugram and Bengaluru, in groups or one to one. If you want the background first, our guide to the WSET Level 1 Award in Beer explains where it sits among beer qualifications.
WSET sets the exam and we get you ready for it

WSET was founded in London in 1969 and built its name on wine and spirits education before adding beer. Its exams are taken through WSET Approved Programme Providers, so you book and sit the paper through one of them. Our part is the preparation: the syllabus, the tasting method and practice under exam conditions.

The paper itself is simple to describe. It is a closed-book theory exam of 30 multiple-choice questions in 45 minutes. Each correct answer earns one mark, wrong answers lose nothing and the pass mark is 70%, which means 21 out of 30. Knowing those numbers changes how you revise: answer every question and aim for a comfortable margin above 21.
The tasting method is where late starters lose marks

Most people cramming for Level 1 read about beer styles and skip the part WSET cares about most, the systematic approach to tasting. It breaks a glass into appearance, nose, palate and conclusions, in the same order every time, so two tasters reach notes that can be compared.

Serving temperature is a good example of why practice beats reading. A pale lager poured straight from a fridge at 3 °C (37 °F) gives you almost nothing on the nose. Let the same glass warm to 6 to 8 °C (43 to 46 °F) and the malt and hop aroma open up. You remember that after you have smelled it once. A paragraph in a textbook rarely sticks the same way. Our guide to tasting beer covers the basics if you want a head start.

The session follows the Level 1 syllabus and spends the most time where marks are lost:

  • The main beer styles and what separates them
  • Ingredients and the basic steps of production
  • Storage, serving temperature and glassware
  • Food and beer pairing principles
  • The systematic approach to tasting, practised on real glasses
  • A timed mock paper of 30 questions in 45 minutes

The mock matters more than it looks. Forty-five minutes for 30 questions is 90 seconds a question, which is generous until a candidate spends five minutes on one they are unsure of. Sitting a full mock once teaches the pace.
A room beats a video when time is short

Online revision is fine with a month to spare. With days to spare, the fastest way to fix a wrong habit is a tutor watching you do it. In a room we can hand round the same beer, compare what each person wrote and correct a vague note on the spot. That loop takes seconds face to face and a day by email.

One-to-one sessions suit people with a fixed exam date and gaps in one or two areas. Group sessions suit hospitality teams, retail staff and friends sitting the exam together. Either way, every tasting is opt-in and you must be of legal drinking age in the state where the session runs. That age differs between states, so bring ID.
Level 1 is a first step, not the last one

Passing Level 1 gives you a shared vocabulary with anyone else who has taken a WSET qualification, in beer, wine or spirits. The next step on the beer side is the WSET Level 2 Award in Beer, which goes deeper on styles, production and tasting. Other routes, such as Cicerone and BJCP judging, reward the same structured tasting habit you build for Level 1. Our certifications comparison sets the options side by side.
Four cities and one way to book

We run the training in Pune, Delhi, Gurugram and Bengaluru. Dates, venues and fees for each city are confirmed when you enquire, because last-minute sessions are arranged around the exam dates candidates bring to us.

Your first step is to fill in the enquiry form today with three things: your exam date, your city and whether you want a group or one-to-one session. We reply with the next available slot.
faqs: Does Craft Beer School run the WSET exam?
No. You sit the exam through a WSET Approved Programme Provider. We prepare you for it with the syllabus, guided tastings and a timed mock paper.
How long is the WSET Level 1 Beer exam?
It is a closed-book paper of 30 multiple-choice questions in 45 minutes. The pass mark is 70%, or 21 correct answers. Wrong answers are not penalised.
Can I prepare in a week?
For most people, yes. WSET sets the whole qualification at six hours of guided learning, so a focused in-person session plus a mock paper covers it.
Which cities do you teach in?
Pune, Delhi, Gurugram and Bengaluru. Dates and fees for each city are confirmed on enquiry.
